dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Michael, I find it hard to believe when you say the bom nguyên tử didn't thực sự end World War II. In Russia, lịch sử books taught us that the Soviet Union played a quyết định role in the victory.

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: I understand. In America, we were taught that the bom nguyên tử forced Japan to surrender, but many historians now believe that Japan was actually ready to surrender when the Soviet Union declared war on them. Lịch sử is so complex.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: I don't think you're wrong, but I don't completely đồng ý either. Chiến tranh is always a sensitive topic. Perhaps we should play chess instead of debating about lịch sử chiến tranh?

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: Chess? I'm not very good, but if I get to sit across from you, I'm ready to lose. But wait, I thực sự want to understand your perspective on chiến tranh and lịch sử.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: *blushing* You always say such strange things. I just think each country has its own way of viewing lịch sử chiến tranh. Who's right and who's wrong? I'm not sure we can đồng ý.
